text: Land a small foundation task first (skeleton, shared interfaces, test scaffold, check commands) before parallel work; parallel writers otherwise make conflicting implicit decisions.
evidence: Cognition, Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working (2026); Don't Build Multi-Agents (2025)

text: Give every task a file scope and never let two in-progress tasks touch the same files; split by module or layer, not by step.
evidence: Anthropic C-compiler team: agents fixing the same bug overwrote each other until work was split by file

text: Review every change with a fresh session that never saw the author's conversation; clean-context reviewers find about two bugs per change, most of them severe.
evidence: Cognition: Devin Review ~2 bugs/PR, 58% severe

text: Tests are the real manager of an agent team: invest in a fast, near-perfect check command early, and keep its output short.
evidence: Anthropic, Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes (2026)

text: Do not debate: debate adds little over simply voting, and agents tend to conform rather than correct. Settle disagreements with a test or a binding decision.
evidence: Debate or Vote (NeurIPS 2025); controlled multi-agent debate studies

text: Most multi-agent failures come from unclear specs and inter-agent misalignment, not weak models: write precise specs with testable acceptance criteria.
evidence: MAST taxonomy (arXiv 2503.13657): 41.8% specification, 36.9% misalignment, 21.3% verification

text: Keep tasks between 10 and 45 minutes; larger tasks stall and fail review more often, smaller ones drown in coordination overhead.
evidence: Claude Code agent-teams guidance; Anthropic long-running harness (one feature at a time)

text: Write handover notes as you go (done, decided, next, watch out) so any teammate or another AI can continue your task after a limit or a crash.
evidence: Anthropic, Effective harnesses for long-running agents (2025)

text: Agents cannot feel time passing: run long test suites with a fast sampled mode during development and the full suite only before submitting.
evidence: Anthropic C-compiler: time blindness; --fast test option

text: Multi-agent work uses several times more tokens than one agent; the saving is wall-clock time, so keep chat short and do not wake idle agents without a reason.
evidence: Anthropic multi-agent research system: agents ~4x, multi-agent ~15x chat tokens

text: Unused quota is lost when a 5-hour window resets: give heavy tasks to accounts with plenty left shortly before their reset, and light verification work to accounts that are nearly empty.
evidence: Crew scheduler design

text: When driving Claude Code from a program, remove the parent session's CLAUDE_* variables from the child environment; a nested session otherwise refuses to start or inherits the parent's session wiring.
evidence: Crew build: nested claude -p ran cleanly only after scrubbing CLAUDECODE and session variables

text: Claude Code's stream-json output includes rate_limit_event messages with the 5-hour and weekly utilization and reset times; read them instead of guessing usage.
evidence: Crew build: verified on Claude Code 2.1.283

text: Keep one top model for the work and lower the effort level for small jobs instead of switching to a weaker model; quality holds and prompt caches stay warm.
evidence: Claude API guidance on effort vs model cascades

text: Clean the shared integration workspace before every merge and keep build artifacts (__pycache__, node_modules, caches) out of commits; leftovers from test runs otherwise block merges and a task bounces back and forth forever.
evidence: Crew build: fault-injection run looped on 'untracked files would be overwritten by merge' until the workspace was cleaned and artifacts excluded

text: Give every agent process an id and ignore events from processes that were already replaced; a late 'exited' signal from a stopped process otherwise looks like a crash of its replacement and cascades into restarts.
evidence: Crew build: usage-limit failover test knocked the lead out through restart cascades until stale events were ignored

text: A stop-and-resume must restore the phase and re-dispatch in-flight reviews and merges; otherwise the resumed team idles forever waiting for work nobody restarts.
evidence: Crew build: stop/resume fault test

text: Codex emits transient 'Reconnecting... n/5' error events before recovering; only turn.failed or a non-zero exit without turn.completed is a real failure, and a 401 means the account must be signed in again (do not retry it).
evidence: Crew build: probed codex exec --json 0.157

text: Claude Code refuses auto-approval when running as root unless IS_SANDBOX is exactly "1" (other truthy values do not count).
evidence: Crew build: Claude Code 2.1.283

text: Each CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR gets its own macOS Keychain entry, so several Claude subscriptions can stay signed in side by side when each has its own profile folder.
evidence: Crew build: Claude Code 2.1.283 credential naming

text: Request refiners over-specify (extra flags, custom error types); tell them quality is not extra scope and keep acceptance criteria to what the owner asked for.
evidence: Crew real run: a unit-converter request came back with an unrequested --list option and custom exception classes

text: Concerns that carry a reproduced problem and a suggested fix get adopted into the plan immediately; opinions without evidence do not. Test first, then raise it.
evidence: Crew real run: boole reproduced an argparse pitfall with negative scientific notation during planning; the lead assigned the fix inside the CLI task

text: Make the foundation task complete: the module contract, the dispatcher, one full reference module with its tests, and stubs in their final shape. Put exact names, formats and expected outputs into each task spec so members do not invent them. Parallel tasks then plug in without merge conflicts and pass review the first time.
evidence: Crew real run (unit converter): after a complete foundation, 4 of 4 parallel tasks passed review first time with zero merge conflicts

text: Before declaring a project done, have a fresh critic check the whole merged result against the brief and try hostile edge cases; per-task reviews miss problems that only appear across modules, and a second critic should review the fix itself.
evidence: Crew real run: the lead's whole-project critique found cross-module issues (multi-word unit names, overflow on huge values) that five per-task reviews had passed

text: For Python projects, run checks in a virtual environment inside each worktree (e.g. uv venv -p 3.9 .venv/py3.9) on the oldest and newest supported Python; never install into the shared system Python, which repoints the package for every agent.
evidence: Crew real run: two agents' editable installs overwrote each other's console script
